title: Login and checkout failures
executive_summary: INC-002 (SEV1, login and checkout failures) began at 09:30Z on 2026-09-05. The investigation status is ROOT_CAUSE_IDENTIFIED, with the most probable explanation being a deployment regression in auth-service 2.14.0 (deploy dep-cbc63772, 2.13.4 to 2.14.0, completed 09:28Z). The release migrated JWT validation to jose-4.2 and refactored the token cache. auth-service logs show "unsupported key type 'EC' in JWKS (validator=jose-4.2, kid=k20)" starting 09:29:00Z (logpat-auth-service-f41941c5). Its error rate rose from a 0.3% baseline to a window mean of about 12.9% (max 29.5%) starting 09:29:00Z (met-auth-service-error_rate-0900-0955). Downstream failures followed in order: api-gateway token-verify 500s from 09:29:03Z (logpat-api-gateway-7c1adbea) and payment-service auth-check 500s from 09:30:08Z (logpat-payment-service-a56d8d43). These failures explain the user logouts and checkout errors. Confidence in this hypothesis is 0.78. The critic approved the result.

hypotheses.description: auth-service 2.14.0 (deployed 09:28Z) introduced a JWT validation regression: the jose-4.2 migration cannot parse EC keys in the JWKS, so token verification returns 500s, which propagate to api-gateway and payment-service and force logouts and checkout failures. Mechanism: Deploy dep-cbc63772 (2.13.4 -> 2.14.0, jose-4.2 JWT validation migration + token cache refactor) completes 09:28Z -> auth-service validates tokens with jose-4.2 -> JWKS entries of type EC raise TokenValidationException 'unsupported key type EC' -> /v1/token/verify returns 500 -> api-gateway (token-verify 500s from 09:29:03Z) and payment-service (auth-check 500s from 09:30:08Z, with retries) fail -> login/checkout 5xx and session invalidation. Latency and timeouts stay flat because failures are fast validation errors.

The deploy may be a coincidence or a contributing factor, since the key change and the deploy are not yet separated. Mechanism: New EC-type signing key(s) appear in the JWKS source (rotation or config) at about 09:29 -> auth-service fetches or caches the set -> token verification for tokens signed with the EC kid raises 'unsupported key type EC' -> 500s propagate to api-gateway and payment-service -> login/checkout failures. Under this hypothesis the deploy is not the trigger, and the rollback of 2.14.0 alone may not restore service.

critic_review.summary: H1 (auth-service 2.14.0 jose-4.2 JWT validation regression) is well supported. The auth-service EC-key errors name validator=jose-4.2, a library version that exists only in 2.14.0, and they first appear at 09:29:00, one minute after the 09:28 deploy completed. A search of auth-service logs from 08:00 to 09:29 for EC errors returned nothing, and no auth-service config changes occur in 08:00-10:00. Error rate moves from 0.3% to about 27% at 09:29 with latency and timeouts flat, which fits fast validation failures. Downstream onsets (api-gateway 09:29:03, payment-service 09:30:08) follow the auth-service onset in the expected order. H2 (independent key change) is not supported: no key or JWKS change is recorded, and the validator version points to the deploy. It can still be a contributing trigger, so the rollback check is worth doing. H3 is rejected: user-service error rate is flat at baseline, and there is no graph path from auth/payment to user-service in the failing flow, and the flag change preceded onset by 19 minutes with no failures.

assessments.reasoning: Onset at 09:29 follows deploy completion at 09:28; errors cite jose-4.2 (only in 2.14.0); no EC errors before 09:29; error rate step change with flat latency; downstream errors follow in order. Remaining gap: rollback confirmation, which is an operational check rather than a blocker.

No JWKS/key-rotation or config change recorded for auth-service 08:00-10:00. The errors are attributed to validator jose-4.2, which points to the deployed code rather than key material. A key change could be a contributing factor only if evidence of new kids appears; treat as an alternative to be ruled out by rollback.

user-service error rate is flat at baseline through 09:55, no call path from auth-service or payment-service to user-service is shown, and the auth errors are JWT key validation failures. The config change precedes onset with no observed failures in the 19 minutes before it.

root_cause_statement: ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED (critic-approved; still an INFERENCE from evidence): deployment_regression in auth-service - auth-service 2.14.0 (deployed 09:28Z) introduced a JWT validation regression: the jose-4.2 migration cannot parse EC keys in the JWKS, so token verification returns 500s, which propagate to api-gateway and payment-service and force logouts and checkout failures.
corrective_actions: Roll back auth-service from 2.14.0 to 2.13.4 (dep-cbc63772) to restore token verification. This is the primary mitigation and also serves as the test that confirms the cause.
After rollback, confirm that auth-service error rate returns to baseline (about 0.3%) and that api-gateway token-verify 500s and payment-service auth-check 500s stop.
Ask users who were logged out to re-authenticate, and check payment charges that failed or were retried between 09:30Z and rollback for reconciliation.
Check whether the JWKS key set changed around 09:29Z (H2). If the key set changed, the rollback may not be sufficient on its own and the key publication must be reviewed.
preventive_actions: Fix the jose-4.2 migration so that it parses EC keys in the JWKS (kid=k20 and any other EC keys), and add a regression test covering every key type published in production before re-release.
Add a pre-deploy compatibility check that validates the production JWKS against the new validator in staging.
Review the token cache refactor for shared-state or Redis side effects, since it shipped in the same deploy as the validator change (alternative explanation noted by the critic).
Stage auth-service changes behind canary or progressive rollout so that a validation regression is caught before full fleet exposure.
monitoring_recommendations: Alert on auth-service error_rate above 1% sustained for 2 minutes, paging on-call. The 09:29Z onset would have been caught within minutes.
Alert on auth-service log pattern 'TokenValidationException' or 'unsupported key type' at any non-zero rate.
Track api-gateway 5xx rate on /v1/token/verify and payment-service upstream auth-service 500 counts as separate dashboards, to show propagation.
Add a post-deploy watch that compares error rate for 30 minutes after each auth-service deploy with the pre-deploy baseline.
Log JWKS key publication and key-set changes as events, so that future key-change questions can be answered from records rather than inferred.
limitations: The assumption that 2.13.4 accepted the same EC keys has been inferred from deploy scope, not directly tested.
The config tool may not record JWKS publication events, so the absence of a key rotation has not been fully confirmed.
The token cache refactor's contribution has not been separated from the validator change.
The 0.78 confidence reflects that the rollback test has not yet been run.
Confidence values are rule-based evidence-strength scores, not calibrated probabilities.
Investigation terminated because: critic verdict APPROVED
conclusion: The most probable root cause of INC-002 is the auth-service 2.14.0 deployment (dep-cbc63772), whose jose-4.2 JWT validation cannot parse EC keys in the JWKS. This causes token verification to return 500s, which propagate to api-gateway and payment-service and produce the observed logouts and checkout failures. The evidence supports this with a clear onset sequence, a validator version that exists only in 2.14.0, and a flat latency profile consistent with fast validation errors. The rollback is the decisive next step. The independent JWKS key-change hypothesis (H2) is not excluded until rollback is tested, and the user-service feature flag (H3) is rejected because user-service error rates were at baseline.
